# Introduction

Having acquired our data (see the [ETL page](etl.qmd)) and spent some time to understand it (see the [EDS page](eda.qmd)), this page will actually employ some machine learning models.

We're using the {tidymodels}^[{tidymodels} R packages ([www.tidymodels.org](https://www.tidymodels.org/))] framework, a collection of R packages for machine learning. In particular, we're using the {tidyclust}^[{tidyclust} R package ([tidyclust.tidymodels.org](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org/index.html))] R package. {tidyclust} is effectively a clustering specific replacement for the {tidymodels} package {parsnip}^[{parsnip} R package ([parsnip.tidymodels.org](https://parsnip.tidymodels.org/))].   

We're going to use a "recipe"^[{recipes} R package ([recipes.tidymodels.org](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/))] to tell {tidymodels}. 

```{r setup}

# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(targets)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyclust)

# Sources all R/*.R same as _targets.R
tar_source()       

# Objects needed from our {taregts} pipeline
tar_load(df_lsoa_all)

# ggplot theme
set_theme(theme_minimal())
```

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: true
%%| code-fold: show

flowchart TD
    df["<b>data</b><br/>df_lsoa"]
    rec["<b>recipe</b><br/>lsoa_rec"]
    spec["<b>specification</b><br/>kmeans_spec"]
    
    rec --> wf["<b>workflow</b><br/>kmeans_wf"]
    spec --> wf

    df --> fit
    wf --> fit["<b>fitted workflow</b><br/>kmeans_fit"]

    fit --> assign["<b>augment</b><br/>extract_cluster_assignment()"]
    fit --> cent["<b>extract results</b><br/>extract_centroids()"]
    fit --> eval["<b>evaluate</b><br/>sse_within_total(), sse_ratio(), silhouette_avg()"]
    df -->|"new_data"| eval
    df -->|"select(LSOA21CD)"| clust["<b>clusters</b><br/>LSOA21CD + cluster"]
    assign -->|"$.cluster, same row order"| clust
```

# Data  

The data frame with candidate variables for clustering is called `df_lsoa`. Notes on the production of `df_lsoa` are in the [ETL page](etl.qmd).  

```{r}
#| label: df-lsoa

# TODO
df_lsoa <- df_lsoa_all
rm(df_lsoa_all)

# glimpse(df_lsoa)
```

# Recipe

Our recipe:  

1. Specifies the key i.e. `LSOA21CD`.  
1. Removes selected variables e.g. `cycle_infra_length_m`.  
1. Normalises numeric data.  

```{r}
#| label: recipe

# LSOA21CD is kept as an ID so it is not used as a clustering predictor
lsoa_rec <- recipe(~ ., data = df_lsoa) |>
  update_role(LSOA21CD, new_role = "id") |>
  step_rm(
    starts_with("cycle_infra_"),
    count_point_n,
    starts_with("mean_aadf_")
  ) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

lsoa_rec
```

# Specification.  

Using the {tidyclust}^[Getting started with tidyclust ([tidyclust.tidymodels.org/articles/tidyclust.html#extract-results](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org/articles/tidyclust.html#extract-results))].  

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-spec

kmeans_spec <- k_means(num_clusters = 6) |>
  set_engine("stats")

kmeans_spec
```

# Workflow

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-wf

kmeans_wf <- workflow(lsoa_rec, kmeans_spec)

kmeans_wf
```


# Workflow fitted

Fit the workflow to the data.  

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-fit

set.seed(1234)
kmeans_fit <- fit(kmeans_wf, data = df_lsoa)
kmeans_fit
```

# Extract results

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-assignment

extract_cluster_assignment(kmeans_fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-centroids

extract_centroids(kmeans_fit)
```

```{r}
#| label: kmeans-augment

# Row order matches df_lsoa, so the LSOA ID stays alongside its cluster
lsoa_clusters <- df_lsoa |>
  select(LSOA21CD) |>
  mutate(cluster = extract_cluster_assignment(kmeans_fit)$.cluster)

lsoa_clusters
```

# Evaluate

```{r}
#| label: evaluate

sse_within_total(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa)
sse_ratio(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa)
silhouette_avg(kmeans_fit, df_lsoa)
```
